title: Tell the terminal what the processor decided

blocks.text: Your gateway connects 1987 terminals to a processor that answers with four-digit action codes. `CodeTranslator` holds a table, written code by code from both networks' lists, and tells each terminal what the processor decided. `answerFor` and `mustReverse` already work on top of `toTerminal`.

The processor's release notes add codes faster than the table is updated, and during last week's upgrade some answers arrived with no action code at all. Operations asks for three things: no terminal hands over goods the issuer may not have approved in full; no cardholder is told their card was refused when it was a system that failed; and no purchase is reversed when the processor plainly refused it.
The tests use a table of their own and codes it doesn't list.

cases.says: a code the table lists is answered with the table's 1987 code, and nothing is reversed
the accepted reversal and the accepted advice, which sit outside the approval category, are answered 00 as the table says
an approval code the table lacks may be partial, so the terminal gets 96 and the purchase is reversed upstream instead of being approved
an error code the table lacks reaches the terminal as 96, a failure, not as a decline of the card
a denial code the table lacks is still a denial, 05, and needs no reversal
an answer with no action code, or one that is not four digits, decides nothing: 96 and a reversal, never a decline

origin.section: 9.5. A Gateway Between Editions Translates Each Code From Both Lists

concepts: A gateway between editions translates code by code from a table; codes off the table fall back on their category as a denial or an error, and an approval it cannot read is answered 96 and reversed.
